preferred_referent: Continuity → Dense Live Feed / Source Text
goal: Fit substantially more real external movement on screen while preserving more useful source text. Keep source identity and multi-axis relations readable, remove oversized per-item controls, and make the source headline itself the traversal action.
next_movement: Normalize provider-specific source text without reducing density: strip RSS/markdown boilerplate, distinguish useful body text from promotional/footer text, preserve native media/discussion relations, and then test shared-event clustering without merging source claims.
walls: Do not put social networks, news sites, video platforms, forums, or other external feeds inside Continuity as owned state.
Do not persist the mixed feed contents by default.
Do not generate substitute posts for unavailable providers.
Do not let high-volume sources define the whole frontage merely because they publish faster.
Do not hide raw chronology; preserve a Latest view beside any balancing projection.
Do not collapse provider, publisher, medium, role, and topic into one source_kind.
Do not duplicate an item merely because it belongs to multiple projections such as News and Video.
Do not erase source identity or external locator during normalization.
Do not turn opening a feed item into work; it creates only a traversal touch unless the user explicitly produces another output.
Do not treat touching or displaying an item as evidence that its claims are true.
Do not call internal systems external sources.
Do not bury live movement beneath the area/system directories on the homepage.
Do not redefine A/B as the feed mixer, identity axes, traversal trace, or portal.

handoff.from: Multi-Axis Live Feed Identity → dense source frontage
handoff.reason: The identity model held, but the rendered audit showed too much vertical chrome and too little source material. The feed now spends substantially more viewport on source text, uses clickable headlines instead of large action buttons, and exposes longer provider excerpts.

unavailable_sources: Bluesky public API returned HTTP 403 from this host

views.balanced: Round-robin across provider streams to prevent high-volume feeds from erasing slower feeds.
views.latest: Strict chronological ordering to expose the actual volume/frequency collision.
views.social: Projects items whose roles include social.
views.news: Projects items whose roles include news regardless of medium/provider.
views.video: Projects items whose medium is video.
views.community: Projects items whose roles include community.

witness.result: The same live item is valid in both News and Video projections without duplication.

fixed: Removed stale dashboard CSS and replaced it with one portal-first stylesheet matching the current HTML.
Moved live internet movement above human-area and local-system directories.
Renamed internal source language to Your systems while reserving External feeds for internet movement.
Made Current trail sticky and rendered a visible Mixed feed → source breadcrumb as touches accumulate.
Kept external source/provider identity visible without converting items into Continuity-owned posts.
Replaced flat source_kind classification with independent provider / publisher / medium / roles / topics.
News and Video filters can now overlap on one Reuters/YouTube item without duplicating it.
Removed the separate large Open source / Watch action row; the live headline itself is now the traversal action.
Raised bounded source excerpt budget from 320 to 640 characters.
Added Reuters/YouTube media descriptions when the provider feed supplies them.
Reduced hero, stream header, filter, trail, card, and side-rail spacing to increase useful movement per viewport.
Collapsed the mobile intro and trail so the first live items appear materially higher on screen.
remaining: Longer source excerpts expose provider boilerplate, raw markdown/link syntax, hashtags, and promotional footer text that still need provider-specific cleanup.
Source role chips are useful but visually crowded on narrow screens.
Multiple sources covering one real event still appear as separate feed items.
The website can record departure from Continuity but cannot observe subsequent cross-site navigation without a browser companion/shell.
Top-level Search and Post controls are still not backed by full Continuity behavior.

human_areas.rule: Human areas remain entrances for what the person is doing. The mixed external feed is movement through the internet, not another human area.

checks: Live headline is the traversal action; no large per-item Open source/Watch row remains.
Reuters YouTube descriptions are projected when present.
Desktop and mobile before/after renders were visually audited.
Mobile intro/trail are compact enough that live movement begins materially higher in the viewport.

density_audit.before: Large per-item action buttons and looser cards spent significant vertical space on chrome.
density_audit.after: Clickable headlines, tighter cards, longer excerpts, and compact trail/header surfaces place substantially more real source movement in the same viewport.
density_audit.tradeoff: The limiting factor is now source-text quality rather than card spacing.
